value.evidence: Draft A directly addresses the brief's core motivation by naming LettuceDetect, specifying its technical foundation (ModernBERT, 4K tokens, 79.22% F1), licensing (MIT), and concrete deliverables (Python packages, Hugging Face demo). It preserves the problem context (context window limits, inference costs) and explicitly invites community feedback on applications and real-time detection—actionable for local LLM enthusiasts. Draft B generalizes the same facts into vaguer language ('supports long input sequences,' 'open license,' 'accompanying software') that obscures the specific capabilities and loses the benchmark result entirely. For a community seeking to evaluate whether to adopt or contribute to LettuceDetect, Draft A provides the factual specificity needed to form an informed opinion; Draft B reads as a generic summary that doesn't equip readers to assess fit or engage meaningfully. Both stay within allowed claims and avoid forbidden ones, but A's precision and concrete detail make it substantially more useful to the stated audience.
